Implementation steps

1. Add integration-backpressure as a cycle-level gate
- Add `ORCH_INTEGRATION_MAX_AHEAD_COMMITS` parsing near the existing integration staleness env vars in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`.
- Default to `10`; validate as a positive integer and fall back to `10` on invalid input.
- Reuse the already-computed `CWS_AHEAD_BY` value from the main poll cycle; do not add a second compare call.
- Introduce a small helper that runs after the eager integration PR has been ensured/reused and before the ready-to-merge loop:
  - if `ahead_by >= ORCH_INTEGRATION_MAX_AHEAD_COMMITS`, add `ai:integration-backpressure` to the tracking issue and mark the cycle as “do not merge more managed PRs into integration”
  - if `ahead_by < ORCH_INTEGRATION_MAX_AHEAD_COMMITS`, remove `ai:integration-backpressure` if present
- Reuse the existing completion-status comment to point operators at the current integration PR (`state.final_merge_pr`) rather than creating a brand-new comment family.
- Keep the gate local to sub-issue merges into the integration branch; do not block validation dispatches, final-PR autofix/review, or the existing final-merge logic.

2. Add the `ai:force-merge` validation-lifecycle bypass
- Hook this into the eager-draft maintenance path in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, not the noop-suspicious PR force-merge sweep near the bottom of the file.
- Conditions:
  - tracking issue has `ai:force-merge`
  - integration PR exists/is open
  - queued orchestrator work still remains (stay in the pre-completion validation lifecycle)
  - current integration SHA has not already been bypassed for this SHA
- Actions for a new SHA:
  - if the integration PR is still draft, promote it to ready
  - post an audit comment on the tracking issue
  - post an audit comment on the integration PR
  - persist one deterministic operator-bypass audit entry keyed by tracking issue + integration SHA
  - store additive state-file idempotency data (for example, last-bypassed integration SHA and timestamp) so repeated ticks on the same SHA do not re-post/re-append
- Reuse the existing validation-status PR-body block if a custom “next action” message is needed; do not invent a second PR-body section.
- Explicit scope guard: do not alter the existing noop-suspicious force-merge fallback block.

3. Use the existing deterministic AI-memory contract instead of inventing a new one
- Follow `ai-memory/schemas/operator_bypass_audit.v1.json` as the source of truth.
- In `scripts/ai_memory_lib.py`, add/finish the library helpers expected by the existing tests/schema contract:
  - `get_operator_bypass_audit(...)`
  - `append_operator_bypass_audit_entry(...)`
- In `scripts/ai_memory.py`, add the matching CLI surface:
  - `operator-bypass-audit get`
  - `operator-bypass-audit append`
- In `scripts/memory_helpers.sh`, add the matching shell wrappers:
  - `memory_operator_bypass_audit_get`
  - `memory_operator_bypass_audit_append`
- Use the tracking-issue audit comment as the canonical `source_comment_id` / `source_comment_url` stored in the bypass record; the PR comment is additional operator-visible trail.

4. Keep GitHub API usage bounded and cache-first
- For backpressure, use the existing per-cycle `CWS_AHEAD_BY` cache.
- For `ai:force-merge` actor attribution, prefer existing in-memory/cycle data first.
- Only if the actor still cannot be derived, do one bounded issue-events lookup against the tracking issue (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/events?per_page=100`) and use the newest `labeled` event for `ai:force-merge`; GitHub’s PR REST resource also exposes the ready/draft state through the `draft` field, which matches the current eager-draft lifecycle. citeturn1view1turn2view0
- Do not add an unbounded timeline/events scan or a second compare probe.

5. Update docs/contracts in place
- `README.md`
  - add `ORCH_INTEGRATION_MAX_AHEAD_COMMITS` to the env-var tables
  - extend the “Atomic final merge” / operator docs to explain:
    - what `ai:force-merge` does
    - that it promotes the eager integration PR early and leaves an audit trail
    - what `ai:integration-backpressure` means
    - that backpressure points operators at the open integration PR and clears automatically below threshold
- `agents.md`
  - append the exact new stable log prefixes introduced by the implementation (at minimum: one for force-merge bypass application and one/two for backpressure enter/clear transitions)

Conflicts / codebase mismatches to call out
- The checked-out ref is partially inconsistent with the issue’s dependency assumptions:
  - `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` already references deterministic validation-history and `/revalidate` memory helpers
  - but `scripts/memory_helpers.sh` on this ref does not currently define those wrapper functions
  - and `scripts/ai_memory.py` / `scripts/ai_memory_lib.py` do not currently expose the matching validation-history / revalidate / operator-bypass helper surface that the schemas/tests expect
- `tests/test_ai_memory_processed_command_entry.py` already codifies the intended operator-bypass library/CLI/wrapper contract, so the implementation should match that contract instead of inventing a new memory shape.
- Historical plan notes use older naming for the bypass primitive; the current repo contract is the deterministic `operator_bypass_audit.v1` schema and should win.

Risks / edge cases
- Same-SHA idempotency: no duplicate `gh pr ready`, no duplicate audit comments, no duplicate memory append.
- New-SHA behavior: the bypass path must be allowed to run again for a later integration SHA.
- If the integration PR is already ready on a later SHA, the implementation should stay idempotent and avoid comment spam while still preserving per-SHA audit semantics.
- Actor lookup miss/API failure: fail open with explicit audit text rather than blocking the poller.
- Backpressure should not oscillate on compare API failure; only transition label state on numeric `ahead_by`.
- Backpressure must not affect the existing noop-suspicious force-merge fallback or the final integration-merge path.
- Backpressure should only block new sub-issue merges into integration, not the already-open integration PR’s review/autofix/validation lifecycle.

Testing considerations
- Extend `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`; do not add a new standalone test script.
- Reuse existing eager-draft/validation-history test setups as the starting pattern.
- Add/extend poller tests to prove:
  - `ai:force-merge` promotes the eager draft PR for the current integration SHA
  - the same SHA is idempotent on the next poll
  - a later integration SHA can trigger one new bypass/audit episode
  - tracking-issue and PR audit trail are visible
  - deterministic operator-bypass audit persistence is written once per SHA
  - backpressure at the threshold blocks ready-to-merge sub-issue PR merges into the integration branch
  - `ai:integration-backpressure` is added at threshold and cleared automatically below threshold
